prompt: A trampoline bounce follows $h = 30t - 5t^2$, with $h$ in centimeters above the mat after $t$ seconds. Using the arc's symmetry, find the MAXIMUM height, in centimeters.
hint: A parabola is symmetric, so its highest point is exactly halfway between the two times when the height is zero.

hints.text: A parabola is symmetric, so its highest point is exactly halfway between the two times when the height is zero.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Test a time: at $t = 2$, $h = 60 - 20 = 40$ cm. To find when it lands, ask when $h$ returns to $0$ and factor out the $t$.
Factor $30t - 5t^2 = 5t(6 - t)$ to see that $h = 0$ at $t = 0$ and $t = 6$. The peak is halfway, at $t = 3$. Put $t = 3$ into the formula.
$h = 30 \times 3 - 5 \times 9 = 90 - 45 = 45$, so the maximum height is $45$ centimeters.

explanation: Find when the jumper is on the mat by factoring: $30t - 5t^2 = 5t(6 - t) = 0$, so $t = 0$ or $t = 6$.
A parabola is symmetric, so the vertex lies halfway between those times, at $t = 3$.
Substitute $t = 3$ to find the height there: $h = 30(3) - 5(3)^2 = 90 - 45 = 45$.
The maximum height of the bounce is $45$ centimeters.

alternativeExplanations.title: Table of the bounce
steps: The heights climb, peak at 45, then mirror back down — the max is 45 cm.

alternativeExplanations.title: Rainbow symmetry
steps: The bounce arc is a rainbow: up-time equals down-time.
In the air from t = 0 to t = 6, so the top is at t = 3.
Plug in t = 3: 90 − 45 = 45 cm at the very top.
